# Host reference for the SO-101 scene, recorded 2026-07-28 on x86_64
# GNU/Linux, gcc 13, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, -ffp-contract=off.
#
# Same contract as baselines/teleop-franka-host-x86_64.txt: a bitwise
# self-lock for THIS architecture, not a cross-architecture claim.
#
# WHY A SECOND TRACE EXISTS, since the Franka's already covers every line
# of shared code: it does not cover the scene. The way a scene loses its
# physics is not a code edit — MuJoCo's <attach> under the default conflict
# policy discards the child model's entire authored <option> block and
# reports no error, measured as all six fields at once. The Franka scene
# uses <include> and can never exercise that. So does this one today, which
# is exactly why the opt_* lines below are worth locking: they are what
# would go red if someone switched this wrapper to <attach> without
# <compiler conflict="merge"/>. See the long comment in
# assets/so101/ar_scene.xml.
#
# The values inherited from so101.xml, verbatim, are timestep 0.005,
# integrator 3 (implicitfast), cone 1 (elliptic) and impratio 10. The last
# two are the gripper's authored friction model.
#
# pos_med_mm ships at 2.23 mm. The same script on this arm gives 6.10 mm at
# w_rot 0.10, 28.91 mm at 0.30 and 53.60 mm at 1.0, so a mistyped row in
# src/robot_spec.c reddens that line while a benign refactor does not.
#
# EXPIRY, stated because none of this has run on a headset: w_rot,
# clutch_scale and the robot's placement are the three numbers most likely
# to move on the first on-device session. When they do, this file is
# re-recorded IN THE SAME COMMIT that changes them, and the commit message
# says which number moved and what was measured.
#
# REGENERATE WITH:
#   ./build/teleop_replay build/so101/ar_scene.xml \
#       > baselines/teleop-so101-host-x86_64.txt
# then RESTORE THIS COMMENT BLOCK BY HAND — teleop_replay does not emit it.
# teleop replay: scripted engage/move/release/recenter/reset
